Assessment adjusted using the May 2021 Financial Stability Report: The FOMC statement is dovish and supportive—policy rate at 0–0.25%, ongoing Treasury and MBS purchases, and explicit forward guidance under average inflation targeting—against a backdrop of strengthening activity and employment and progress on vaccinations. However, the FSR tempers this optimism by flagging elevated asset valuations and compressed risk premiums, lingering stress in commercial real estate, leverage and risk-management weaknesses at some nonbank financial institutions, and structural funding vulnerabilities (for example, money market funds and Treasury market fragility under stress). While banks appear well capitalized and overall conditions remain accommodative, these vulnerabilities raise downside tail risks to the outlook. Net tone remains moderately positive but more risk-aware than the policy statement alone would suggest. Accordingly, the sentiment score is revised slightly lower to reflect FSR-identified vulnerabilities.
